question: A molecular biologist is studying the roles of different types of ion channels regulating cardiac excitation. He identifies a voltage-gated calcium channel in the sinoatrial node, which is also present throughout the myocardium. The channel is activated at ~ -40 mV of membrane potential, undergoes voltage-dependent inactivation, and is highly sensitive to nifedipine. Which of the following phases of the action potential in the sinoatrial node is primarily mediated by ion currents through the channel that the molecular biologist is studying?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Voltage-gated calcium channel" -> "activated at ~ -40 mV" -> "influx of calcium ions" -> "depolarization of sinoatrial node" -> "Phase 0 of action potential" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Voltage-gated calcium channel" -> "activated at ~ -40 mV" -> "calcium influx" -> "contributes to depolarization" -> "Phase 0 primarily mediated" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Voltage-gated calcium channel" -> "sensitive to nifedipine" -> "inhibition reduces calcium influx" -> "affects depolarization" -> "Phase 0 involvement" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Voltage-gated calcium channel" -> "voltage-dependent inactivation" -> "calcium influx decreases" -> "repolarization not primarily mediated" -> "Phase 3 less likely" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Voltage-gated calcium channel" -> "activated at ~ -40 mV" -> "calcium influx" -> "sustains depolarization" -> "Phase 0 of action potential" -> 90%
analysis: The voltage-gated calcium channel described is likely the L-type calcium channel, which is activated at around -40 mV, undergoes voltage-dependent inactivation, and is sensitive to nifedipine. In the sinoatrial node, the L-type calcium channels are primarily responsible for the rapid depolarization phase of the action potential, known as Phase 0. This phase is characterized by the influx of calcium ions through these channels, leading to the depolarization of the cell membrane.
